_comment: Best-effort USD estimates for cost tracking ONLY, never authoritative billing. Token models use inputPer1M/outputPer1M. imageModels and documentModels use the explicit billing basis shown. Any absent model or unsupported option records cost as unknown rather than zero.
_source: Azure Retail Prices API (https://prices.azure.com/api/retail/prices, 2023-01-01-preview) for Azure BFL Flux Models, Azure Mistral Models Global Standard meters, and Azure Content Understanding document/contextualization meters. GPT-6 Astra uses Microsoft's official Global Standard short-context launch pricing (https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/blog/gpt-6-astra-frontier-intelligence-for-work-now-generally-available-in-microsoft-foundry/), verified 2026-09-06 while its retail meters await publication. GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna use Microsoft's official Global Standard short-context launch pricing (https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/blog/gpt-6-astra-sol-and-luna-for-production-agents-in-microsoft-foundry/), verified 2026-09-23 while their retail meters await publication. GPT-5.5 uses the Azure Retail Prices API Global Standard short-context meters '5.5 ShortCo inp Gl' and '5.5 ShortCo opt Gl' (product Azure OpenAI GPT5, eastus2 and swedencentral, effective 2026-05-01), verified 2026-09-23. MAI-Thinking-1 comes from the official Azure MAI registry asset. Claude comes from Anthropic's official Microsoft Foundry pricing documentation.
_caveats: Flat rates cannot express every meter dimension. Long-context, cache, priority, Data Zone, regional, batch, reference-image, annotation, and provisioned variants may differ. Astra's Global Standard long-context rates are $20 input/$75 output per million tokens rather than the short-context $10/$50 estimate recorded here. Global Standard long-context rates are $4/$15 for GPT-6 Sol, $0.20/$0.75 for GPT-6 Luna and $10/$45 for GPT-5.5 rather than the short-context estimates recorded here; their Data Zone Standard rates carry a 10% US or 20% EU premium for GPT-6 Sol/Luna and a 10% premium for GPT-5.5. FLUX.2 estimates use output megapixels; FLUX.1 uses one image. MAI-Image-2.5/Pro/Flash, MAI-Image-2.6/Flash, gpt-image-2, and gpt-image-1-mini remain cost-unknown because no unambiguous Azure retail meter is published. gpt-image-2.5-flare and gpt-image-2.5-sunburst also remain cost-unknown: their Azure retail meters (verified 2026-09-23) bill text and image tokens per million, which this per-image/megapixel image book cannot map. Mistral OCR 4 annotation pricing is excluded because this app requests OCR only. Content Understanding page meters are recorded separately by minimal/basic/standard usage; standard versus advanced contextualization is taken from the service's own contextualizationTokens and advancedContextualizationTokens usage properties, never from a locally authored analyzer label.
_claudeSource: Verified 2026-09-20: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing#claude-in-microsoft-foundry-pricing and #model-pricing. Opus 5 $5/$25, Sonnet 5 $2/$10 standard USD/MTok; US DataZoneStandard applies 1.1x, including cache reads. Rates are estimates, not a bill cap. Cache writes remain cost-unknown when their duration is not evidenced; no caching is requested by the adapter.

gpt-realtime-1.5.notes: Published OpenAI reference estimates, not verified Azure billing rates. The realtime ledger has no complete modality/cache breakdown or bounded session envelope. Do not flatten these into models or use them for hard admission.

gpt-realtime-2.1.notes: Verified public Azure retail Gl meters for this model and eastus2 only, not a subscription price quote or actual billing validation. Modality/cache usage and a bounded session envelope remain incomplete, so runtime cost and hard admission stay unknown. Do not flatten these references into models. Image meters do not enable a new image-input surface.

gpt-realtime-2.1-mini.notes: Verified public Azure retail Gl meters specific to 2.1-mini; no rate is copied from full 2.1 or an older mini. Retail DZ meters do not prove a subscription DataZoneStandard offering. These references do not establish actual billed usage, a flat runtime price, a session bound, or an image-input capability.
